newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Nearly 40 die in Brazil rains, thousands homeless.
newsitem.headline: Nearly 40 die in Brazil rains, thousands homeless.

text.p: Heavy rains in the Brazilian states of Minas Gerais and Rio de Janeiro have killed at least 39 people and made 11,900 people homeless, local radio and television said on Saturday.
Minas Gerais has been hardest hit after several days of rains that led to widespread flooding and mudslides.
In the historic town of Ouro Preto, 60 miles (96 km) from the state capital of Belo Horizonte, 12 people were killed after being buried in a mudslide. Only a 4-year-old child escaped, Globo said.

Globo also showed pictures of emergency services trying to revive a 6-year-old girl after she had been pulled from the muddy debris of her destroyed home in Belo Horizonte. The girl later died in a hospital. One woman was brought out alive from the same house but four other family members were killed.
"We have to start all over again. Everything's finished, we have nothing left. Life for us now will be something else," said one young man surveying his wrecked home before bursting into tears.

Three hydro-electric stations have had to open their gates because of the deluge of rainfall resulting in evacuations of several regions. Some 200 people have been injured and 6,900 have lost their homes in the state, local radio said.

At least 5,000 people were homeless in the north of Rio de Janeiro state, where rains have caused widespread damage to property and agriculture. There have been no reports of any deaths caused by the rains so far.

A state of emergency has already been declared in several towns, with heavy rains forecast to continue in both states over the weekend. Emergency services could not be reached to comment on the number of deaths and homeless.
